c.tagline: Highveld capital of misty mountains, craft markets, and royal culture.

taxi.fareNote: Metered taxis are rare; fares for kombis are fixed by route, while private taxis negotiate a fixed price before the ride, especially for airport or intercity trips.

emergency.note: Fire: 933. Response times can be slow outside the capital; private medical evacuation insurance is recommended.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

avoid.reason: No strict no-go zones, but stay out of the central bus rank and downtown streets after dark, when muggings occur.
Pickpocketing around the main market and bus rank; take taxis rather than walking at night.

hood_desc: The compact commercial capital with government offices, malls (Swazi Plaza, The Mall) and the main business hotels; convenient base for city errands and onward travel.
A lush valley 15-20 minutes from Mbabane with spas, casinos, craft markets and the country's densest cluster of resorts; suits travelers wanting comfort and easy access to Mlilwane and Lobamba.
A creative, laid-back farming valley south of Ezulwini known for House on Fire, Malandela's and weekend markets; suits artsy travelers and those attending Bushfire Festival.
A cool pine-forest escape in the highveld about 25 minutes from Mbabane, centered on the historic Foresters Arms; suits hikers and those wanting a quiet countryside retreat.
The wildlife sanctuary and surrounding hills just outside the capital, offering rustic lodges and beehive huts among zebra and antelope; suits nature lovers and budget/backpacker travelers.

water.note: Municipal water is treated and locals drink it, but many travelers still opt for bottled water to be safe.

transit.pay: Fares are paid in cash directly to the driver or conductor in local currency (Emalangeni); there is no electronic fare card system. Kombis leave when full from ranks near Swazi Plaza/Mbabane bus rank, and fares are set per route.
transit.hours: Buses and kombis generally run roughly 6am-6/7pm; little to no public transport after dark, so taxis or pre-arranged transport are used at night.
transit.note: Mbabane has no rail network; minibus kombis are the dominant form of local and intercity transport.

bus: Kombis (shared minibus taxis) to Manzini, Ezulwini, Piggs Peak and other towns

transit.m: Shuttle van (Eswatini Air complimentary/paid shuttle, ~1 hr)

tip.r: Not obligatory; rounding up or 10% at sit-down restaurants is appreciated, especially where a service charge isn't already included.
